title: Simple rectangular wrap
subtitle: A beginner-friendly DK rectangle in garter stitch — the most relaxed knitting possible.
excerpt: A plain garter-stitch rectangle in DK yarn: cast on, knit every row until the wrap is long enough, cast off. No increases, no decreases, no pattern to track. Finished size approximately 45 cm wide by 170 cm long. About 250 g of DK yarn. A first-project-worthy cast and the most useful piece in a knitter's wardrobe.
sourceNotes: A plain garter-stitch rectangle is the fundamental knitting project, taught in every beginner resource. The construction predates any identifiable publication. No specific source.

glossaryTerms.definition: The simplest knit stitch fabric: every row is knitted on both sides. Produces a ridged, elastic fabric with equal horizontal and vertical stretch. The ridge count visible on one side equals half the total row count.

A two-strand cast-on that simultaneously places stitches on the needle. It creates a firm, elastic cast-on edge and leaves a long yarn tail (the 'long tail') which is incorporated into the cast-on row itself.

content.text: rectangle in DK yarn: cast on, knit every row, cast off. There is nothing else to this pattern and that is entirely the point. Finished size approximately 45 cm wide by 170 cm long.

A garter rectangle is the first thing most knitters make and also one of the last things they stop reaching for. The fabric is perfectly reversible, slightly elastic, and lies flat without curling. It also shows off hand-dyed or gradient yarns beautifully. Budget about 250 g (about 550 m / 600 yards) of DK yarn.

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, measured after washing. At gauge 99 stitches gives 45 cm width. 748 rows gives 170 cm length. If your gauge is looser, say 20 stitches per 10 cm, cast on 90 stitches for a similar width.
, cast on 99 stitches. Measure out a tail approximately 85 cm long before starting. Begin with the tail over your thumb and the working yarn over your index finger.
Knit every row until the wrap measures 170 cm from the cast-on edge. There is nothing else to track. Use a row counter or tally if you want to check your progress.

Standard knit bind-off. Work loosely: slip the first stitch, k1, then pass the slipped stitch over. Continue to the last stitch; cut yarn and pull through. The bind-off edge should be neither tighter nor looser than the cast-on edge.
Every 50 rows: count to confirm 99 stitches remain. Garter stitch should not grow or shrink unless a stitch was added or dropped.

Stitch count increasing slowly: a yarn-over was accidentally created at the end of a row by leaving the yarn forward before knitting the last stitch. Always hold the yarn in back (the far side of the work) before beginning each knit stitch.
Loops at the selvedge: stitches at the end of the row were slipped rather than knitted. Knit every stitch including the very first and the very last on every row.
Hand wash in cool water or machine wash on a wool/gentle cycle at 30°C if the yarn ball band allows. Lay flat to dry.

Add a stripe: every 20 rows, switch to a contrasting colour. Carry the unused yarn up the selvedge rather than cutting and re-joining. Stripes introduce colour management and are the natural next step after a plain rectangle.
